content.title: Accessibility
content.summary: The City of Arvada is committed to preventing discrimination based on disability in its services, programs, and employment practices, in accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act and Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act. The City actively works to enhance technology accessibility through its Digital Accessibility Plan and welcomes suggestions for improvement. Individuals can request accommodations or modifications and are encouraged to submit their requests at least 48 hours prior to any time-sensitive events.
content.body:
## Notice Under the Americans with Disabilities Act (“ADA”) and Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act (“Section 504”)

In accordance with the requirements of Title II of the ADA and Section 504, the City of Arvada will not discriminate on the basis of disability in providing City services, programs, or activities. The City also strives to effectively communicate with individuals with disabilities and will, upon request, provide auxiliary aids and services leading to effective communication. The City of Arvada will also provide requested, reasonable accommodations or modifications. The City is not required to take any action that would fundamentally alter the nature of its programs, services, or activities, or that would impose an undue financial or administrative burden.

## Equal Opportunity and Non-Discrimination in Employment

The City of Arvada does not discriminate based on disability in its hiring or employment practices.  The City complies with all regulations promoted by the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission under Title I of the ADA.

## City of Arvada Technology Accessibility Statement

The City of Arvada is committed to advancing the technology accessibility of the City’s information and communication technology (ICT).  In support of this commitment, the City is making good faith progress on its Digital Accessibility Plan.  The City’s Digital Accessibility Plan aligns with Version 2.1, Level AA, of the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG 2.1 AA); is updated annually; and guides the City’s efforts to remove accessibility barriers for ICT in active use.  The City believes that removing accessibility barriers to ICT  increases the accessibility of City programs, services, and activities for everyone, regardless of ability.

As the City’s digital accessibility efforts are ongoing, the City welcomes suggestions for improvement. The City also recognizes the importance of providing reasonable accommodations and modifications when needed and as appropriate under any applicable accessibility standards.  Please use one of the contact methods listed in the “Request an Accommodation or Modification” section below to provide suggestions for accessibility improvement, report inaccessible ICT, to request a reasonable accommodation or modification, or to request reasonable assistance in submitting a suggestion or request.  The City will timely respond to any submitted suggestion or request.  You may also review and utilize the City’s Grievance Procedure located below.

[City of Arvada Digital Accessibility Progress Report](/1086)

[City of Arvada Technology Accessibility Plan](/1333/City-of-Arvada-Digital-Accessibility-Pla)

## Map Accessibility

Many of our pages feature embedded maps or links to maps that we have created using ArcGIS, Esri's comprehensive geospatial platform. While we strive to make our maps as accessible as possible, we may have encountered certain limitations in the software itself. Please visit [Esri's Accessibility Conformance Reports](https://www.esri.com/en-us/legal/accessibility/conformance-reports) page for more information.

## Request an Accommodation or Modification

Anyone may submit a request for an accommodation or modification through one of the following methods listed below.  The methods below may also be used to request reasonable assistance in submitting a request or to submit a suggestion for improvement.  If a request for a reasonable modification or accommodation is for a time-sensitive event, **please submit the request no later than 48 hours before the event.** Please do not use this form to submit a complaint or grievance related to alleged discrimination, which must be submitted using the Grievance Procedure below.  The ADA Coordinator or their designee will timely respond to all suggestions and requests.

- By submitting the [ADA City of Arvada Request or Suggestion Submission Form](https://arvada-forms.app.transform.civicplus.com/forms/40459)
- By regular mail to:
  - City of Arvada  
    Attn: ADA Coordinator  
    8101 Ralston Road  
    Arvada, CO 80002
- By email to: [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#39584b4f585d58585d5879584b4f585d5817564b5e)
- By telephone to: 720-898-7611 or 303-319-9503 (available Monday-Friday between the hours of 8:00 a.m. and 5 p.m. M.S.T. excluding observed City holidays; voicemails will be promptly returned)
- By relay Colorado (Deaf and Hard of Hearing individuals) call 7-1-1

## Grievance Procedure Under the ADA

This Grievance Procedure may be used by anyone who either feels that they have not been able to access a City facility, program, service, or activity because of a lack of accessibility or feels that they have been discriminated against because of their disability.  This Grievance Procedure is not intended to be used to submit internal, employment-related claims, suggestions to improve digital accessibility, or to request an accommodation or modification.  For suggestions or requests relating to digital accessibility, please refer to the information listed under the header reading “City of Arvada Technology Accessibility Statement.”  Please note that all written communications and documents received by the City according to the Grievance Procedure will be retained for a minimum of three years from the date of receipt.

### Grievance Procedure

- **Step 1:** If possible, any person who believes they have been discriminated against on the basis of disability in the provision of City services, programs, benefits, or activities should attempt to resolve the issue with the City director responsible for providing the service, program, benefit or activity.  If this is not possible or the resolution attempts failed, the person may proceed to Step 2 of this Grievance Procedure.
- **Step 2:**Within 60 calendar days of the alleged discrimination occurring, or within 60 calendar days in which the alleged discrimination should have been known, a person may submit ADA Title II Grievance Form.  If the person is unable to complete the ADA Title II Grievance Form, the person may submit a written grievance through one of the contact methods listed below.  The written grievance must contain the complainant’s name, contact information, location of the alleged discrimination, and a description of the alleged discrimination.  Please note that if a verbal reporting method is used, a City representative will use reasonable efforts to document the grievance.
  - By submitting the [ADA Title II Grievance Form](https://arvada-forms.app.transform.civicplus.com/forms/32089)
  - By regular mail to:
    - City of Arvada  
      Attn: ADA Coordinator  
      8101 Ralston Road  
      Arvada, CO 80002
  - By email to: [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#64051612050005050005240516120500054a0b1603)
  - By telephone to: 720-898-7611 or 303-319-9503 (available Monday-Friday between the hours of 8:00 a.m. and 5 p.m. M.S.T. excluding observed City holidays; voicemails will be promptly returned)
  - By relay Colorado (Deaf and Hard of Hearing individuals) call 7-1-1
- **Step 3:**The City’s ADA Coordinator or their designee will meet with the complainant within 14 calendar days of receiving the grievance to discuss any possible resolutions unless the ADA Coordinator and complainant agree to a different time.  The ADA Coordinator and the complainant will communicate to determine an accessible format for the meeting, which may occur by telephone, virtual conference, or in-person meeting.  If the alleged discrimination involves the ADA Coordinator, the Director of Public Works will substitute for the ADA Coordinator throughout this Grievance Procedure.
- **Step 4:** Within 28 calendar days of the meeting from Step 3, the ADA Coordinator will respond to the complaint in writing, and where appropriate, in a format reasonably accessible to the complainant.
- **Step 5:**  If the ADA Coordinator’s response does not satisfactorily resolve the grievance, the complainant must file a written appeal with the City Manager no later than 14 calendar days after the ADA Coordinator sent the Step 4 response.  The City Manager or their designee will respond to an appeal within 14 calendar days of receiving the appeal.  The response will be in writing, and where appropriate, in a format reasonably accessible to the complainant.  The response is a final agency decision.

## Browser Accessibility Information

Many popular browsers contain built-in accessibility tools.

- [Chrome Accessibility Information](https://www.google.com/accessibility/all-products-features.html)
- [Firefox Accessibility Information](https://www.accessfirefox.org/)
- [Microsoft Edge Accessibility Information](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/accessibility/)
- [Safari Accessibility Information](https://support.apple.com/accessibility)

## Additional Plug-ins

Adobe Reader is required to view and print PDF documents that appear on this website.

- To download this program for free, visit the [Adobe website](https://get.adobe.com/reader/).
- To read PDF documents with a screen reader, please visit the [Adobe Reader Accessibility website](https://helpx.adobe.com/reader/using/accessibility-features.html) which provides useful tools and resources.

## Supported Assistive Technology

- Latest Version of [JAWS](https://www.freedomscientific.com/Products/Blindness/JAWS) for Windows
- Latest Version of [NVDA](https://www.nvaccess.org/) for Windows
- Latest Version of [VoiceOver](https://www.apple.com/accessibility/vision/) for Mac OS X
- Keyboard-Only Navigation
